mainTopic: Is a כותבת הגסה bigger than a כביצה, and do fruits need a סוכה?
overview: The גמרא compares two measures: the כותבת הגסה (a large date, the amount that makes one liable for eating on יום כיפור) and the כביצה (an egg's volume, the amount that must be eaten in a סוכה). The סוכה stories suggest that two dates are less than a כביצה, so how can one large date be more? רבי ירמיה answers that date pits are very large, and רב פפא backs this up with a folk saying. רבא answers differently: the dates were allowed outside the סוכה only because fruit never needs a סוכה. The גמרא defends רבא against a ברייתא about figs and grapes. It then rejects an attempted proof for him from a ברייתא about מיני תרגימא. רב זביד argues the opposite: a כותבת הגסה is smaller than a כביצה. His proof from בית שמאי's measures for שאור and חמץ is rejected. The גמרא then proves his point from רבי יהודה's rule about זימון: a כביצה satisfies a person, while a כותבת only settles the mind. The amud ends by opening a ברייתא from רבי, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: An egg's volume of food must be eaten in the סוכה
steps.stepSummary: From the story of רבי צדוק, who ate less than a כביצה outside the סוכה, the גמרא learns that a full כביצה must be eaten in the סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that an egg's volume needs a סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a simple inference from the story it just quoted: רבי צדוק ate outside the סוכה only because his food was less than a כביצה. This is a setup line for the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since less than a כביצה may be eaten outside, a full כביצה must be eaten inside the סוכה. This gives us a fixed measuring stick, the כביצה, which the גמרא will now compare to the size of dates.

keyTerms.meaning: This implies; the opposite case is that…
Requires a סוכה (must be eaten in a סוכה)

phrases.english: This implies: an egg-bulk requires a sukkah.
phrases.notes: We learn this from רבי צדוק, who ate less than a כביצה outside the סוכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the סוכה story quoted on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כביצה of food must be eaten in the סוכה.

steps.title: How can one large date be bigger than an egg?
steps.stepSummary: The stories imply that two pitted dates are less than a כביצה, so how could one כותבת הגסה with its pit be more than a כביצה?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think the כותבת הגסה that the חכמים spoke of is bigger than a כביצה, there is a problem. Two dates without their pits are not even a כביצה. Can one large date with its pit really be bigger than a כביצה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that the יום כיפור measure (a large date) is bigger than an egg. From the earlier story it seems that even two dates are smaller than an egg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier story showed רבן גמליאל's two dates did not require a סוכה by law, so two dates together must be less than a כביצה. If two dates are less than an egg, it seems impossible that one date, even with its pit, could be more than an egg. The attack is on the comparison of sizes between the two measures.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it would enter your mind (to say)
A large date (the יום כיפור eating measure)

steps.confusionAlert: The 'two dates' are eaten without pits, while the כותבת הגסה is measured with its pit. That difference is the key to the answer in the next step.

phrases.english: And if it should enter your mind
that the large date they spoke of
is larger than an egg-bulk,
now, two dates without their pits
phrases.notes: Learned from the earlier story about the dates.

phrases.english: are not an egg-bulk,
a large date with its pit
is it really larger than an egg-bulk?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ כּוֹתֶבֶת הַגַּסָּה שֶׁאָמְרוּ יְתֵירָה מִכְּבֵיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the כביצה measure from step 1 to attack the claim that a כותבת הגסה is bigger than an egg.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the כותבת הגסה is larger than a כביצה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two pitted dates are less than an egg, so one date with its pit should surely be less than an egg too.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: Yes, the pit makes the difference
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה accepts both facts: two pitted dates are less than a כביצה, yet one large date with its pit is more than a כביצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: Yes. Two dates without their pits are not a כביצה, and still one large date with its pit is bigger than a כביצה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers that there is no contradiction, because both statements are true at the same time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hidden point is that a date pit is very big. Removing the pits shrinks the dates so much that two pitless dates are smaller than one whole date with its pit.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said: Yes,
two dates without their pits
are not an egg-bulk,
yet a large date with its pit
is larger than an egg-bulk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2 by accepting both of its facts.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual clarification: the pit is so large that both claims are true together.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed impossible for one date to be bigger than an egg if two dates are smaller than one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The pit adds so much volume that one whole large date is more than a כביצה.

steps.title: רב פפא: A folk saying proves pits are huge
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא supports רבי ירמיה with a saying: in two קב of dates, more than one קב is pits.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is what people say: 'Two קב of dates, one קב and more is pits.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings a common saying to show that רבי ירמיה is right about date pits being so large.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If more than half the volume of dates is pit, then taking the pits out cuts each date by more than half. That explains how one whole date can outsize two pitted ones.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say (a folk saying)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי ירמיה and רב פפא, a כותבת הגסה is bigger than a כביצה, because date pits are very large.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said,
this is what people say:
two kav of dates
one kav of pits and more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי ירמיה's answer in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: רבי ירמיה's claim that date pits are very large.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A popular saying that pits make up more than half of a quantity of dates.

steps.title: רבא: Those dates were allowed outside because fruit needs no סוכה
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the question differently: the dates in the סוכה story were allowed outside because fruit never needs a סוכה, not because of their size.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There, the reason is that dates are fruit, and fruit does not need a סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to the קשיא from step 2. He says the story does not prove anything about the size of dates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in step 2 assumed the dates were allowed outside because they were less than a כביצה. רבא says the real reason is that fruit is never required in a סוכה, whatever its size. So we cannot learn from that story that two dates are smaller than an egg.
steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a new halachic question that the rest of this passage examines: does fruit require a סוכה?

phrases.english: Rava said: There, this is the reason:
because they are fruit,
and fruit does not require a sukkah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 2's קשיא in a different way from רבי ירמיה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removes the premise: the story is explained by a different reason, not by size.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dates were allowed outside because they were less than a כביצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dates were allowed outside because fruit never needs a סוכה, so the story says nothing about their size.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי ate figs and grapes outside only as a snack
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says רבי ate fruit outside the סוכה as a snack, which implies that a fixed meal of fruit would need a סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged רבא: רבי said, 'When we learned Torah with רבי אלעזר בן שמוע, they brought us figs and grapes, and we ate them as a snack outside the סוכה.' This implies that a snack is allowed outside, but a fixed meal is not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא with a ברייתא suggesting that fruit does need a סוכה when it is eaten as a real meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'as a snack' seem to be added for a reason. They imply that if the fruit were eaten as a fixed meal, it would need a סוכה. That contradicts רבא's rule that fruit never needs a סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא)

phrases.english: They raised an objection: Rebbi said:
When we were learning Torah
with Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua,
they brought before us figs and grapes,
and we ate them as a casual eating outside the sukkah.
A casual eating, yes,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is drawing this out of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: a fixed meal, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's rule from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that fruit does not require a סוכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's words 'as a snack' imply that a fixed meal of fruit would need a סוכה.

steps.title: Read it: We ate them like a snack
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the ברייתא as saying fruit is always treated like a snack, so it may be eaten outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: we ate them like a snack, outside the סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by slightly re-reading the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'As a snack' is not a condition that excludes a fixed meal. It describes what eating fruit always is: like a snack. Fruit never counts as a fixed meal, so it never needs a סוכה.
steps.confusionAlert: The added letter כ ("like") changes everything: it is not 'a snack and not a meal' but 'fruit is like a snack'.

phrases.english: Say: we ate them like a casual eating
outside the sukkah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'A snack' implies that a fixed meal of fruit would need a סוכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Eating fruit is always considered like a snack, so it is permitted outside the סוכה.

steps.title: Or: The snack was the bread eaten with the fruit
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the fruit was eaten as a fixed meal, and the 'snack' refers to a little bread eaten with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: we ate the fruit as a fixed meal, and we ate some bread with it as a snack, outside the סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to defend רבא from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the word 'snack' refers to the bread, not to the fruit. The fruit was a full meal and was still eaten outside, which actually fits רבא. The bread was only a small amount, so it was also allowed outside.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say (an alternative answer)

steps.whatToRemember: Both answers keep רבא's rule: fruit does not need a סוכה, even when eaten in large amounts.

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
we ate them as a fixed meal,
and we ate bread as a casual eating
together with them, outside the sukkah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: אֲכַלְנוּם אֲכִילַת קֶבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 6, alongside step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-assigning the phrase 'snack' to the bread instead of the fruit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fruit was a fixed meal eaten outside; only the bread was a snack.

steps.title: Possible support for רבא from מיני תרגימא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a ברייתא supports רבא: it says one may complete his meals with מיני תרגימא, and does not mention fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say a ברייתא supports רבא? 'Therefore, if he completed with מיני תרגימא, he has fulfilled his obligation.' If fruit needed a סוכה, it should say 'fruit'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to bring a proof for רבא's rule from a ברייתא about completing the required eating in the סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists foods that count toward the סוכה obligation and mentions מיני תרגימא, not fruit. If fruit were important enough to need a סוכה, the ברייתא would have mentioned it. Its absence suggests fruit is not a סוכה-requiring food, as רבא says.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this supports him?
Let it teach (it should have said)

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him:

phrases.aramaic: לְפִיכָךְ, אִם הִשְׁלִים בְּמִינֵי תַרְגִּימָא — יָצָא.
phrases.english: Therefore, if he completed with types of sweets, he has fulfilled his obligation.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ פֵּירֵי בָּעוּ סוּכָּה,
phrases.english: And if it should enter your mind that fruit requires a sukkah,
let it teach 'fruit'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבא, the גמרא now looks for positive support for him.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that fruit does not need a סוכה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that names מיני תרגימא, not fruit, as completing the סוכה eating.

steps.title: Rejection: מיני תרגימא means fruit
steps.stepSummary: The proof fails because מיני תרגימא itself means fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are מיני תרגימא? Fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by explaining the term in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof rested on the claim that the ברייתא left fruit out ('let it teach fruit!'). If מיני תרגימא itself means fruit, then fruit was not left out, and that argument collapses. So the ברייתא is no support for רבא.

phrases.english: What are 'types of sweets'? Fruit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the support for רבא entirely.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed מיני תרגימא excludes fruit, but the term actually means fruit.

steps.title: Or: It speaks of a place where fruit is rare
steps.stepSummary: A second rejection: the ברייתא mentions sweets only because it speaks of a place where fruit is uncommon.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: it speaks of a place where fruit is not common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second reason why the ברייתא does not prove רבא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא named sweets only because in that place people ate sweets and not fruit. Fruit could count just the same, so leaving it out proves nothing. רבא's view stands, but without this support.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא holds fruit does not need a סוכה. The ברייתא of figs and grapes does not disprove him, and the ברייתא of מיני תרגימא does not prove him.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
in a place where fruit is not common.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: בְּאַתְרָא דְּלָא שְׁכִיחִי פֵּירֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second rejection of step 9's proof, alongside step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the support for רבא entirely.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Leaving out fruit may only reflect a place where fruit was rare, not a halachic difference.

steps.title: רב זביד: The large date is smaller than an egg
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד states that the כותבת הגסה is less than a כביצה, and points to a משנה where בית שמאי give different measures for שאור and חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: the large date that the Sages spoke about is less than an egg-bulk. As we learned in a משנה, בית שמאי say: for leaven (שאור) the measure is an olive-bulk, and for leavened bread (חמץ) the measure is a date-bulk.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד disagrees with the earlier assumption and says a large date is smaller than an egg. He names the משנה he will build his proof on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא treated the כותבת as bigger than a כביצה. רב זביד flips this. He does not prove his point yet. He only quotes the source, and the proof comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A large date; the amount of food that makes a person liable for eating on יום כיפור
An egg-bulk, a standard halachic volume
Sourdough starter, used to make other dough rise
An olive-bulk, the usual minimum measure for most איסורים

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up שאור and חמץ. שאור is the strong sourdough starter. חמץ is ordinary leavened bread. בית שמאי give שאור the smaller measure.

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said:
The large date that they spoke of
is less than an egg-bulk.
phrases.notes: This reverses the earlier assumption that a date is bigger than an egg.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna: Beit Shammai say:
Leaven: an olive-bulk;
leavened bread: a date-bulk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about the size of the כותבת, disagreeing with the earlier assumption that it is bigger than a כביצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כותבת הגסה is smaller than a כביצה.

steps.title: Why do בית שמאי give two different measures?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls an earlier discussion that asked for the reasoning behind בית שמאי's split measures.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed this: what is the reason for בית שמאי's view?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It brings up an old question about בית שמאי's reasoning, because the answer is needed for רב זביד's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To prove anything from the measure 'a date', we first have to understand why בית שמאי chose a measure bigger than an olive for חמץ. This question opens that explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And we discussed it', introducing an earlier analysis of a source

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
What is the reason of Beit Shammai?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בָּהּ: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the משנה quoted in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why do בית שמאי give חמץ a larger measure than שאור?

steps.title: The Torah wrote both words to show different measures
steps.stepSummary: If שאור and חמץ had the same measure, the Torah would only need to write חמץ, and we could learn שאור by a קל וחומר. Writing both shows they have different measures: שאור a כזית, and חמץ a ככותבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the Torah write only 'חמץ' and not need to write 'שאור'. I would reason: if חמץ, whose leavening power is weak, is forbidden at an olive-bulk, then שאור, whose leavening power is strong, should certainly be forbidden at that amount too! Since the Torah wrote them separately, it teaches you that the measure of one is not the measure of the other. שאור is an olive-bulk, and חמץ is a date-bulk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the Torah mentioned both שאור and חמץ to show they have different measures. Since שאור keeps the usual כזית, חמץ must have a bigger measure, a ככותבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר would already give שאור the same measure as חמץ, so writing שאור separately would be extra. The extra word teaches that the measures differ. Since שאור is the stronger one and stays at a כזית, חמץ gets a larger measure.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One', meaning the Torah or ה׳
All the more so; the language of a קל וחומר
Since He separated them (wrote them separately)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key point for רב זביד: בית שמאי were looking for a measure bigger than a כזית for חמץ.

phrases.english: Let the Merciful One write "leavened bread,"
and He would not need "leaven,"
and I would say:
If leavened bread, whose leavening is not strong,
is forbidden at an olive-bulk,

phrases.aramaic: שְׂאוֹר שֶׁחִמּוּצוֹ קָשֶׁה — לֹא כָּל שֶׁכֵּן?
phrases.english: then leaven, whose leavening is strong, all the more so?
phrases.notes: A קל וחומר: if the weaker item is forbidden at a כזית, the stronger one surely is.

phrases.english: Since the Merciful One separated them,
it taught you

phrases.aramaic: שִׁיעוּרוֹ שֶׁל זֶה לֹא כְּשִׁיעוּרוֹ שֶׁל זֶה.
phrases.english: that the measure of this is not like the measure of that.
Leaven at an olive-bulk,
and leavened bread at a date-bulk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Torah wrote both words to show different measures. שאור stays at a כזית, and חמץ gets a larger measure, a ככותבת.

steps.title: If a date were egg-sized or bigger, they would have said 'egg'
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד's proof: בית שמאי wanted the next measure above a כזית. If a כותבת were bigger than or equal to a כביצה, they would have said כביצה. So a כותבת must be smaller than a כביצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think the large date is bigger than an egg-bulk: after all, בית שמאי are looking for a measure bigger than an olive-bulk, so let them teach an egg-bulk! And even if the two are equal, let them teach an egg-bulk! Rather, doesn't this prove that a date is less than an egg-bulk?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out the proof for רב זביד. בית שמאי chose 'a date' and not 'an egg', so a date must sit between an olive and an egg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי only needed something bigger than a כזית. If an egg were smaller than a date, the egg would be the closer step up and they would have used it. If the two were equal, they would have used the more familiar egg. Since they chose the date, it must be smaller than an egg.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind (to say)
They are equal to each other
Learn from this; a proof is established

phrases.english: And if it should enter your mind
that the large date they spoke of is bigger than an egg-bulk,
after all, Beit Shammai
are searching for a measure larger than an olive-bulk,
so let them teach an egg-bulk.
And also, if they are equal,
let them teach an egg-bulk!
phrases.notes: The egg is the more common, familiar measure.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not so? Learn from it:
a date is less than an egg-bulk.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ כּוֹתֶבֶת הַגַּסָּה שֶׁאָמְרוּ יְתֵירָה מִכְּבֵיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reasoning from step 14 (that חמץ needs a measure above a כזית) to prove רב זביד's claim from step 12.
steps.raayaObject: רב זביד's claim that a כותבת is smaller than a כביצה
steps.raayaSupportSource: בית שמאי's choice of 'ככותבת' rather than 'כביצה' as the measure for חמץ

steps.title: Maybe they meant an ordinary date, or just picked one of two equal measures
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Maybe only a large date is bigger than an egg while an ordinary date equals an egg, and בית שמאי meant an ordinary one. Or maybe a date and an egg are equal and the משנה just chose one.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know this? Perhaps I can really tell you that the large date they spoke of is bigger than an egg-bulk, but an ordinary date equals an egg-bulk. Or even if they are equal, the משנה simply chose one of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down רב זביד's proof by giving two other ways to read בית שמאי's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First answer: בית שמאי said only 'a date', not 'a large date', so they meant an ordinary date, which is the same as an egg. The large date of יום כיפור can still be bigger. Second answer: even if a date equals an egg, nothing forced the משנה to pick 'egg', so choosing 'date' proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: From where (is this proven)? Introduces a rejection
And he chose one of them

steps.whatToRemember: רב זביד claims a כותבת is smaller than a כביצה, but his proof from בית שמאי is rejected. בית שמאי's 'date' could be an ordinary date equal to an egg, or the משנה may simply have picked one of two equal measures.
steps.confusionAlert: Notice the difference between 'כותבת הגסה' (a large date, the יום כיפור measure) and a plain 'כותבת' (the measure in בית שמאי's משנה). The rejection depends on these being two different sizes.

phrases.english: From where?
Perhaps I could actually say to you
that the large date they spoke of
is bigger than an egg-bulk,
but an ordinary one equals an egg-bulk.
phrases.notes: בית שמאי said plain 'date', not 'large date'.

phrases.english: Or alternatively, they are equal,
and he chose one of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from בית שמאי. It does not disprove רב זביד's claim itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed בית שמאי's 'date' is the same as the large date, and that they had to use 'egg' if the two were equal. Neither assumption is required.

steps.title: A new source: the minimum amount of food for a זימון
steps.stepSummary: After the first proof was rejected, the גמרא brings a new source. It is a מחלוקת between רבי מאיר (a כזית) and רבי יהודה (a כביצה) about how much food obligates a זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, prove it from here: How much must one eat to be part of a זימון? A כזית, says רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: a כביצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the rejected proof from בית שמאי and brings a different source. It quotes a teaching about the minimum amount of eating that obligates a זימון. This step sets up the new proof, which is completed a few steps later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אֶלָּא tells us the previous proof is set aside. This source is useful because רבי יהודה ties a fixed size, the כביצה, to the idea of being 'satisfied.' That link becomes the key to comparing a כביצה with a כותבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, from here (introduces a new proof after the old one failed)
They join together for a זימון, the group invitation to say ברכת המזון
The invitation that three people who ate together make before ברכת המזון

phrases.english: Rather, prove it from here:
How much must one eat to be included in a zimmun?
An olive-bulk; these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: The Hebrew עַד here means the minimum amount, 'as little as.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: an egg-bulk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proof from בית שמאי, which step 16 rejected, with a new source.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a כותבת הגסה is smaller than a כביצה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about the minimum amount for a זימון

steps.title: What is the basis of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reasoning lies behind the two different amounts.
steps.simpleTranslation: On what point do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind each opinion. This is a setup question that prepares the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depends on why רבי יהודה chose a כביצה, not just on the fact that he did. So the גמרא needs his reasoning spelled out first.

keyTerms.meaning: On what point do they disagree?

phrases.english: On what point do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the two opinions quoted in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What each תנא learns from the פסוק ״וְאָכַלְתָּ וְשָׂבָעְתָּ וּבֵרַכְתָּ״

steps.title: Two readings of 'you shall eat and be satisfied'
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר splits the פסוק: 'you shall eat' means eating, and 'be satisfied' means drinking. Eating is always a כזית. רבי יהודה reads the words together: eating that brings satisfaction, which is a כביצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds: 'And you shall eat' refers to eating, and 'and be satisfied' refers to drinking. Eating is a כזית. רבי יהודה holds: 'And you shall eat and be satisfied' means eating that satisfies, and that is a כביצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the two opinions come from two ways of reading the same פסוק about ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, 'eating' keeps its usual Torah meaning of a כזית. For רבי יהודה, the eating must be eating that satisfies, and he sets that amount at a כביצה. This gives us a fixed rule: a כביצה is enough to satisfy a person.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall eat and be satisfied' (דברים ח:י), the source of ברכת המזון

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds:
'And you shall eat' refers to eating,
'and be satisfied' refers to drinking;
and eating is with an olive-bulk.
And Rabbi Yehuda holds:
'And you shall eat and be satisfied' means eating that brings satisfaction,
and what is that? An egg-bulk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18 by explaining each side's reading of the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה requires eating that satisfies, which is a כביצה. So a כביצה satisfies a person.

steps.title: If an egg-bulk satisfies, a date must be smaller
steps.stepSummary: Suppose the כותבת הגסה were bigger than a כביצה. Then a כביצה, which is smaller, would not reach the amount that settles the mind, even though it fully satisfies a person. That makes no sense, so the כותבת must be smaller than a כביצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you thought the large date the חכמים spoke of is bigger than a כביצה, then a כביצה would be less than the amount that settles the mind. But a כביצה actually satisfies a person, so can it be that it does not even settle his mind?! Rather, learn from this that the large date is smaller than a כביצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses רבי יהודה's rule to prove רב זביד's point. It does this by showing that the opposite idea leads to a contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור, a person is liable for eating a כותבת הגסה because that amount 'settles the mind' (מיתבא דעתיה), meaning it ends the feeling of affliction. Satisfying someone is a stronger effect than merely settling his mind. So the amount that satisfies, a כביצה, must be bigger than the amount that only settles the mind, the כותבת.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it would enter your mind (introduces an assumption the גמרא is about to show is impossible)
His mind is settled, meaning the affliction of יום כיפור is removed
Rather, is it not so? Learn from this (draws the conclusion of a proof)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that 'settling the mind' is the bigger effect. Satisfying a person (שביעה) is the stronger effect, so it needs the larger amount.
steps.whyThisMatters: This proof backs up רב זביד's claim from step 12, after his own proof from בית שמאי was rejected in step 16.

phrases.english: And if it should enter your mind
that the large date they spoke of is bigger than an egg-bulk,
now, an egg-bulk actually satisfies a person,
would it not settle the mind?!
Rather, is it not so? Learn from this:
the large date they spoke of is smaller than an egg-bulk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי יהודה's rule from step 19 to the size of the כותבת.
steps.raayaObject: רב זביד's claim that a כותבת הגסה is smaller than a כביצה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's rule that a כביצה satisfies, set against the idea that a כותבת only settles the mind

steps.title: Egg-bulk satisfies, date-bulk settles the mind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sums up the two levels: a כביצה satisfies a person, while a כותבת only settles his mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: An egg-bulk satisfies; a date-bulk settles his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the conclusion as two short rules, one for each measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels of effect: being fully satisfied, which takes a כביצה, and having one's mind settled, which takes a כותבת. Since settling the mind is the weaker effect, the כותבת is the smaller measure.

keyTerms.meaning: The size of a date, the measure for being liable for eating on יום כיפור

steps.whatToRemember: A כביצה satisfies (שביעה). A כותבת הגסה only settles the mind (יתובי דעתא). So the כותבת הגסה is smaller than a כביצה.

phrases.english: An egg-bulk satisfies;
a date-bulk settles his mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the result of the proof in step 20.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The כותבת הגסה is smaller than a כביצה. A כביצה satisfies, while a כותבת only settles the mind.

steps.title: Opening a new teaching from רבי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא in the name of רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא). The content of the ברייתא continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי says:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only opens a new ברייתא; its actual teaching appears on the next amud. It is a setup line that prepares the next move in the sugya.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תַּנְיָא signals a teaching of the תנאים from outside the משנה. Its content, which comes on the next amud, will add new information to the discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: Rabbi says:
phrases.notes: The statement itself continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new source after the proof about the כותבת was completed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated; it continues on the next amud.
